I’m a long time pheonix volunteer.. I have been a volunteer for the past three years with Phoenix and I absolutely love the community. The community has been a blessing for me but as much as I’ve tried I can’t get behind this app. 

I have noticed members complaining about how the app isn’t easy to navigate, how they have trouble signing up for events now, how the app now is too similar in name to the cable network “free form “ and how much confusion there is between the Phoenix and NewForm. 

For example: a newcomer comes in and asks where the NewForm members are not where are the Phoenix members are meeting up. I explain the best way I can but they are still confused. 

As a volunteer I find switching back from “member“ to “ volunteer” is frustrating. I sometimes can’t even find members to add as participants in my events and it’s damn near impossible to find the place to get support or give feedback despite their being countless issues. 

I find it harder to find actual events to attend thus I haven’t been going to events as much. Since the launch of the NewForm app I have only been to a handful of events while under the Phoenix app I would attend events all the time. With the events I have hosted before the app switch we would have 36 attendees every event and now it’s 10 if that. 

I feel the new app is a cause of the lower attendance numbers. If I dislike using it as a volunteer how do the members feel without an easy way to voice their displeasure? 

It’s hard to write this review as I do love the community and appreciate the people , the donors , the staff , and volunteers that make all of these amazing things possible but I feel like it would be a disservice if I gave a 5 star review to an app when it’s the community that is 5 stars and the app is a 2 at most . 

I do not write this to be mean towards the developers of the app as I can only imagine how hard they’ve worked and I ask that these issues I addresses be acknowledged and not fall onto deaf ears.

reviews.text:
NEWFORM UPDATE HONEST FEEDBACK. I love The Phoenix, but the NewForm update in March 2025 made the app experience worse. The creators did not consult users before they released it, and many of the reviews here after March are dismal. The NewForm website runs like a marketing ad, and the app seems more interested in appearances rather than functionality. The entire point and function of a recovery community app is to find meetings and events, get the relevant information, and sign up easily. On this, the NewForm app fails. Luckily they haven’t changed too much on the volunteer interface side of things, but I dread the day that they do. I second my fellow reviewers in the following feedback:

- Half of the photos are irrelevant to the events that they are paired with, and the overly large stock photos are a waste of space. I spend too much time scrolling to find the information I need because the photos get in the way.
- Same thing with the large “Meetings, Wellness, Fitness, Social Activities” icons and the “Activities” buttons on the Experience page. Get rid of it. Or make that a drop-down bar to conserve space. Or keep it as a “Filters” button, like it is on the calendar page. When I click on the Experiences page, I want to know the events in my area up front.
- The font is too light and missable across the entire app. We have people of all ages in recovery and if the print is so tiny I can barely find it, then I can’t imagine how difficult it is to locate for our older or nearsighted members. Particularly the font for Duration, Capacity, and Intensity Levels is TINY. Again here, the stock image gets in the way.
- Minor note. I think Phoenix events should be labeled “The Phoenix” rather than just “Phoenix,” because it looks confusing when a city is listed right beforehand or members are trying to distinguish between the city and the organization.
- In the Events Near You page, include the option for a monthly calendar for people who plan ahead instead of requiring them to scroll week by week. This is also useful for people who travel and want to find Phoenix events in other cities. See the Apple Calendar monthly view of Google Calendar for ideas.

I would check the old Phoenix app multiple times daily but because of the new formatting, user interface, and reduced functionality, I am on the app less and find myself going to fewer events. I appreciate what NewForm is trying to do in connecting multiple recovery communities, but a significant amount of user experience was lost in the process.

Great Idea. I’ll start with the technical side: the app freezes constantly, making it nearly unusable.

On a conceptual level, I was drawn to the idea of this being a community for sober individuals not necessarily as an extension of AA, but as a broader space where people could connect in different ways. I was excited by the potential for activities like museum trips, group dinners, walking meetups, or creative pursuits like painting, art classes, and photography. It sounded like a great way for people to step away from the bar scene and form meaningful connections.

Unfortunately, the reality of the app was nothing like what I envisioned. It feels far more limited in scope than I expected, and the technical issues just add to the frustration.

At this point, I’m likely going to uninstall it it’s disappointing when the concept doesn’t live up to the execution, and on top of that, it simply doesn’t function.

1 Star due to functionality issues, 5 Stars for the idea and potential.

reviews.text: Such an amazing idea for people in recovery. I love this idea, however with that being said it seems like it focuses mostly on major cities. New Hampshire as a whole has almost no community for this platform. There is nothing offered in New Hampshire but I believe it could be an amazing way for persons with a history of issues to find support and guidance. I also believe this could be a path of the highest form to help deliver people like myself from darkness. I can’t wait for this to expand and get bigger in my area. I just think it’s unfortunate that the northeast has such a small community to the north. Our country and people need more stuff like this it has so much potential to help our nation learn, accept, and move forward from the pains of the past. I just wish the Covid stuff did not have such a large impact on everything as human interaction in person and out of technology is a major part of the fabric of humanity. I hope to see more community events in the north where people get together in real life. This is an excellent opportunity to help us find our way.
